title: Which change matters more: the number in front or the power?
description: Mumbai's population of two crore is written as two times ten to the power seven. Changing the two to three adds one crore, but changing the seven to eight makes ten times as many people. The book also writes Kohima's population with only the digits we are sure of. Keeko doubts that changing the two to three is the bigger jump.
teaching_notes: One idea: the power of ten says how big a number is, and the digits in front only refine it. Watch for students who think a bigger digit in front beats one more in the power.

source: Mumbai's population is about 2 × 10 to the power 7. Compare
video_script.why: A change in the power of ten changes a number far more than a change in the digit in front. The number of digits in front also shows how sure we are.
video_script.substitution: Turn each version into crores and compare it with two crore; then move the point to leave one digit in front.
video_script.anchor: Mumbai's population of two crore written as 2 × 10⁷, and Kohima's population
video_script.wrong_answer: changing the two to three makes the bigger jump
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko compares the jump from 2 to 3 with the jump from 7 to 8 and thinks the first is bigger. In crores it is 2 to 3 against 2 to 20.
video_script.payoff_line: Changing the power of ten changes the size far more than changing the number in front

final_answer.value: changing the power multiplies by 10, changing the number in front multiplies by 1.5; Kohima is about 1.42 × 10 to the power 5
final_answer.spoken: Three crore is one and a half times two crore. Twenty crore is ten times two crore. Kohima is about one point four two times ten to the power five.

maths_rules: the slip: the jump 2 to 3 adds 1 crore, the jump 7 to 8 adds 18 crore
